attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated as his conclusion.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the premise (specific instructions succeed) and the exclusive 'only one explanation' wording. It is correctly a causal claim about the original Imagen failure.

contract.note: The claim says there is only one explanation, so it is fair to require that rival causes be ruled out. Treating understanding as whether the semantic roles are kept and used is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: A firsthand demonstration from May 2022 backs only the premise that more specific prompts can produce the scene. It does not establish the exclusive cause of the failure.
This study tests Stable Diffusion 2.1, a different model. It suggests training priors as a rival mechanism but cannot settle anything about the original Imagen.

reviews.rationale: The premise has partial support in e1. No evidence tests the original Imagen in a way that separates a failure to interpret the prompt from conditioning, generation or sampling causes. The exclusive causal claim is neither shown nor refuted by the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion. The common-sense hypothesis he rejects came from Ambrogioni, but the rejection is Marcus's.

semantics.note: A faithful negative causal claim. The categorical 'at all' is kept implicitly by the plain negation.

contract.note: Reading 'common sense' as a plausibility preference is broader than Ambrogioni's refusal hypothesis, but it is a reasonable reading. Under the narrow refusal reading the rewording demo would lean toward supporting the claim, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Rewording improves success, which undercuts an unconditional refusal. It does not rule out a contributing plausibility preference, and no sampling rates are given.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is one demonstration with no sample counts. No controlled original-Imagen test separates plausibility effects from wording effects, so the categorical claim that common sense played no part is not settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own conclusion in his post.

semantics.note: A faithful claim about where the failure sits: language-to-image mapping rather than generation. It is scoped to the horse-and-astronaut example.

contract.note: Marcus did not specify where the line between generation and conditioning lies. The contract's reading is reasonable, but the result depends on where that boundary is drawn.

evidence.note: A May 2022 demonstration that a minimal prompt change can succeed. It shows some capacity to draw the scene but does not locate the cause of the original failure.

reviews.rationale: The demonstration shows the scene can be produced, but no component-level or controlled test on the original Imagen pins the failure on language-to-image mapping or rules out generation. The causal location is unresolved.

semantics.note: The flat assertion about the original Imagen is rendered faithfully. 'Has no idea' is vague but firm.

contract.note: The behavioural reading (no systematic, usable competence with these concepts) is an ordinary, fair plain reading of a firm statement.

evidence.note: The original Imagen paper describes DrawBench and alignment results. It has no test of weight, mass or density competence.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no controlled evaluation of the original Imagen on weight, mass or density. The paper is context only, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted on this evidence.
